summary: Mesir wat, an Ethiopian red lentil puree adapted from whats4eats: red lentils simmered until they puree themselves with a fried paste of onion, garlic and ginger and a paprika, turmeric and cayenne spice base; about 40 minutes, thick enough to scoop with injera, serves 4 as part of a larger meal.
glance: 4 as part of a larger meal
2 cups red lentils, simmered until fully pureed
thick enough to stand up a little on a spoon, a little thicker than applesauce but not like hummus
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan with oil instead of butter
yield: 4 as part of a larger meal
faq: What is mesir wat?
A simple and nourishing puree of red lentils with ginger, onions and spices. The technique isn't so different from an Indian dal, but it's made thick enough to pick up directly with injera.
What is injera?

A slightly sour and spongy flatbread that serves as both plate and eating utensil in Ethiopian food. If you have access to an Ethiopian grocery or restaurant, fresh injera is easy to come by; making your own is a bit of a project.
What if I don't have injera?
It would still be delicious served with rice, or thinned slightly into soup.
Why red lentils?
They rapidly puree themselves when simmered. Stir occasionally to avoid scorching on the bottom and add more water if it gets low; add water if too thick or cook a little longer if too thin.
How do I make the spice paste?

Puree the onion, garlic and ginger. Fry the paprika, turmeric and cayenne in the butter or oil for 30 seconds, add the onion mixture and fry about 10 minutes until rather dry and lightly browned, then scrape it into the lentils with about 1/2 teaspoon of salt.

summary: Tagliatelle in white truffle cream sauce: heavy cream reduced about 5 minutes with Parmigiano and at least 5 grams of fresh white truffle grated in with a microplane, rested 15 minutes or more off the heat, then tossed with fresh tagliatelle; serves 2 as dinner or 4 as a first course. Includes the author's first experience with white truffles at about $4,000 a pound.
glance: 2 as dinner or 4 as a first course
1 1/2 cups cream, 3 ounces Parmigiano, at least 5 grams fresh white truffle
infuse the grated truffle in the cream at least 15 minutes (15-30) so the flavor can develop
yield: 2 as dinner or 4 as a first course
faq: How much do white truffles cost?

At DeLaurenti's in Seattle's Pike Place Market they cost $4,000 a pound at the time of the post, about $8 a gram. Even 5-6 grams flavors enough pasta or eggs for 2-4 people, so the cost is about that of a middling restaurant meal.
How do white truffles differ from black?

To the author black truffles are more cleanly aromatic while whites have a pungent characteristic a little like garlic. He thought he might prefer black, which cost only about a fifth as much, but the jury was still out.
Should truffles be cooked or grated on top?

Most of the reading he did suggested infusing black truffles into sauces and risottos while reserving white truffles for grating or slicing on a finished dish. Grated on scrambled eggs with lots of butter, they didn't thrill him; the parmesan cream sauce with a 15-30 minute infusion was astonishing.
How do I make the sauce?

Reduce the cream in a small skillet at a simmer about 5 minutes until slightly thickened, remove from the heat, stir in most of the parmesan, grate in the truffle with a microplane (don't waste a hair), cover and let rest off the heat at least 15 minutes.
How do I finish the dish?

When ready to eat, boil the pasta, reheat the sauce gently over the lowest possible simmer, drain the al dente pasta into heated bowls, toss with the sauce and top with more parmesan, sea salt and pepper.

summary: Double-crust pizza with broccoli raab, ricotta and caramelized onions: a thick Sicilian-style pie of two 12-inch dough rounds filled with a pound of ricotta, onions caramelized at least an hour, fully wilted bitter greens, crushed red pepper and orange zest, vented and baked on a stone preheated to 475°F; serves 4.
glance: enough for two 12-inch rounds (2 1/2 cups flour, 11.25 ounces / 318 grams), potato-bread dough or any pizza dough
1 pound fresh ricotta, 2 large caramelized onions, 1 pound broccoli raab cooked about 15 minutes, orange zest
faq: What inspired this pizza?

Mario Batali's Sfincione di Patate, a Sicilian double-crust pizza with a potato-bread dough filled with ricotta and salami. The author skipped the pig and made something thicker, with a deep pile of caramelized onions, wilted bitter greens, crushed red pepper and orange zest.
Can I use other greens?

Any bitter green you like, or even spinach for a milder pie. The key is that they must be fully cooked and tender (the author calls it "hammered"), so chewiness doesn't interfere with the crust and ricotta. Fennel and artichoke hearts would also be amazing.
What dough should I use?

Mario's potato-bread dough works great but is very soft and wet and hard to stretch without tearing, so use a rolling pin and plenty of flour. Or use any pizza dough scaled to 2 1/2 cups of flour, or buy pre-made dough for two 12-inch rounds.
Is it a good first pizza?
The author says no: it's big and heavy and a bit challenging to get in and out of the oven, though a showstopper. A safer option is to build and bake it in a rectangle right on a baking sheet.
Can I prepare parts ahead?
The onions can be caramelized the day before and refrigerated; cook them over medium-low heat at least an hour, lowering the heat if they begin to burn.

summary: Cheese course with maple pickled pears: a diced Bosc pear tossed with a microwaved cider vinegar, maple syrup, salt and pepper mixture and rested 15 minutes (or overnight) to serve alongside two or three room-temperature cheeses; serves 4 in 15 minutes plus a brief rest.
glance: 2 tablespoons cider vinegar, 2 tablespoons grade B maple syrup, microwaved 1 minute, tossed with 1 Bosc pear
two or three kinds, about 3 ounces total per person, served at room temperature
faq: How should I serve a cheese course?
At room temperature: let the cheese sit out of the refrigerator, covered, for 1 to 2 hours depending on size. Served cold, the complex flavors you paid for are masked.
How much cheese and how many kinds?

For small dinner parties keep it to two or three options, quality over quantity. Three ounces total per person is sufficient, though you may need to buy more to have a respectable-looking chunk. Contrast soft, semisoft and hard cheeses from cow's, sheep's or goat's milk.
Why a cheese course?

The author says it can be a fitting end to any meal: lingering over small portions of beautiful cheeses with a thoughtful condiment and maybe a glass of port or sherry can feel more intimate than a sweet dessert.
What else goes with cheese?
Good honey, preferably with honeycomb; spiced nuts; perfectly ripe fresh figs; or a bit of marmalade. Keep it simple and don't overpower the cheese.
Can I keep the pickled pears?
They can be refrigerated overnight; drain off the pickling liquid before serving, and leftovers can go into grilled cheese sandwiches.

summary: Caramel apple brioche French toast, a work-in-progress dessert styled like a slider: fried brioche squares layered with caramel sauce, a sauteed apple slice, thin slices of well-aged cheddar, flaky salt and maple whipped cream; serves 6.
glance: caramel sauce, brioche French toast, sauteed apple, aged cheddar, maple whipped cream, flaky sea salt
12 brioche squares (2 x 2 x 1/2 inches) soaked about 5 minutes and fried in oil
12 thin slices well-aged cheddar, put on the apple while still warm enough to melt
faq: Where did the idea come from?

From the cheddar-battered onion rings with stout chocolate malt: while reviewing that recipe for the cookbook, the author thought of serving it with a grilled apple slider on brioche French toast. The flavors work as he wanted but the proportions and presentation need work to really resemble a burger.
Why cheddar on a dessert?
It works as a reference to a burger and because lots of folks like cheddar on apple pie. The author doubled the cheddar in this recipe version; get it on the apple while it's warm enough to melt.
What is the maple whipped cream?
1 cup heavy cream beaten with 3 tablespoons of grade B maple syrup (more flavorful than grade A) and a pinch of salt to stiff peaks, or prepared for a whipped cream dispenser, then chilled.
How do I make the apples?
Melt 4 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat and saute 1/2-inch-thick peeled, full-cut round slices (no core) until tender and browned on both sides.
How do I assemble each serving?

About 2 tablespoons of caramel on each plate, a brioche slice, 2 more tablespoons of caramel, an apple slice, two thin slices of cheddar, a few flakes of salt, a second brioche piece and a dollop of maple whipped cream; serve immediately.

summary: Lemony white beans with grilled onions: 6 cups of warm cannellini tossed with charred diced sweet onions, olive oil, the zest and juice of 2 lemons, a little preserved lemon, sage, rosemary, jalapeno, yellow bell pepper, parsley and chives; serves 12 as a side, good warm or at room temperature.
glance: 6 cups cooked white beans such as cannellini, drained and warm
zest and juice of 2 lemons plus 1/2 preserved lemon, interior only
a few days in the refrigerator, flavor continues to improve
faq: What is the flavor of this salad?

Basically Italian, with a bit of preserved lemon sneaked in for a Middle Eastern twist. If you don't have preserved lemon, add another fresh lemon. Go easy with preserved lemon for general audiences: some folks think it tastes like Lemon Pledge in large quantities.
Why grill the onions?
Grilling adds another hit of flavor: slice into thick circles and grill until fairly charred, then dice. Use a barbecue, grill pan or cast iron skillet.
Why warm the beans?
Heat (or cool) the beans to a very warm temperature so they absorb the flavors; you can cook the beans or open a can, drained thoroughly.
How can I serve it?
As a potluck dish, a side salad, the main event of a light lunch, smashed a bit as a dip, or hot as the base layer of an entree plate.
What was it made for?
A Seattle food blogger brunch, where the author expected it to go well with a Yemenite flatbread called lachooch that reminded him of a thicker Ethiopian injera.

summary: Warm winter greens and bread salad, a winter panzanella: braised greens squeezed dry, chopped and tossed in garlic and chili oil, over torn dark-toasted rustic bread dressed with olive oil and lemon juice, topped with Parmesan and finishing salt; a few minutes of active time, serves 1 as a main or 2-3 as a side.
glance: 1 as a main course or 2-3 as a side salad
2 big handfuls winter braising greens, covered with 1/4 cup water and cooked until thoroughly tender
2 slices rustic white bread, toasted rather darkly
right away, before the bread gets soggy
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the Parmesan
yield: 1 as a main course or 2-3 as a side salad
faq: Where did the idea come from?

The author had leftover braised greens from a dish he tested at Cafe Flora, which became a breakfast composed while the frying pan was heating. He thinks it would be nice as a warm salad for a wintry meal: a winter panzanella, great with a soup.
How do I cook the greens?

Remove the coarsest stems, rinse, and cook in a covered pot with 1/4 cup of water and a pinch of salt over high heat for a few minutes, then simmer, checking that there's still a bit of water, until thoroughly tender. Carefully squeeze out most of the water and chop to bite size.
How can I change it?
Different greens, different bread, lemon zest, caraway seeds, whatever suits your mood and pantry.
How do I assemble it?

Toast the bread darkly for flavor; sizzle the minced garlic and chili flakes in a tablespoon of olive oil for a few seconds, add the greens and toss with a light seasoning of salt; tear the bread into a bowl, drizzle with oil and lemon juice (or vinaigrette), top with the greens and garnish.
Why eat it right away?
The bread gets soggy as it sits.

summary: Quick refrigerator pickled onions in two minutes: thinly sliced half-rings of red, white or sweet onion covered with rice vinegar, salt, sugar and optional spices like fennel seeds or citrus zest, shaken and chilled; makes about 1 cup, shown on an adobo tofu taco and a bagel with cream cheese.
glance: 1 onion, about 1 cup rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 1/2 teaspoon sugar
the author uses them for at least a few days in the refrigerator
faq: What do I do with pickled onions?

They pair well with anything creamy or fatty that wants a vinegary, pungent counterpoint: almost any sandwich with cheese, tacos (like adobo tofu tacos), bagels with cream cheese, or tossed with cucumber or cabbage for a quick salad.
How should I slice the onion?
Thinly, crosswise, making half-rings rather than slices; they absorb the flavor better this way.
Which onion is best?
Red, white or sweet onions; yellow is okay but the author's least favorite.
How can I flavor them?
Add seasoning depending on your mood: fennel seeds, peppercorns, coriander seeds, chili flakes, citrus zest. The author's most recent batch had 1/2 teaspoon of fennel pollen, which he calls amazing.
Do the onions have to be fully covered by the vinegar?

No: they wilt enough in the vinegar to be covered by the next day. Shake well and refrigerate. The author doesn't know officially how long they are safe to keep, but uses them for at least a few days.

summary: Raw onion chutney in the style of Indian restaurants in the Northeast US: finely diced onion soaked 30 minutes to tame its bite, then mixed with black mustard seeds, cumin and cayenne bloomed in oil plus tomato paste, vinegar and salt; vegan, makes 1 1/2 cups in 30 minutes (10 active).
glance: 1/2 white or sweet onion, very finely diced (1 1/2 cups), soaked 30 minutes
2 teaspoons black mustard seeds, 1/2 teaspoon cumin, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne
faq: What is this chutney?
A raw onion chutney the author ate almost daily at Indian restaurants in Providence, Rhode Island as a college freshman. He has rarely seen it outside the Northeast and didn't see it in Delhi.
Who will like it?
If you don't care for raw onions you won't like it, but if you crave sweet, pungent crunch it's addictive. It goes well with curries and even better with fritters and pakora.
Why soak the onion?
Soak the finely diced onion in a generous amount of water for 30 minutes. Don't skip it: it removes a bit of the harsh bite.
How do I make the spice mixture?

Heat the oil, cook the black mustard seeds about 30 seconds until they pop and turn gray, add the cumin and cayenne, and ten seconds later (before the cumin can burn) add the tomato paste, vinegar and salt.
How do I finish it?
Drain the onion thoroughly, stir in the tomato mixture (and 1-2 drops of red food coloring if desired), then taste and adjust: you may like more vinegar, salt or cayenne.

summary: Mujadara, Middle Eastern rice and lentil pilaf: 3 pounds of onions caramelized slowly (about 65 minutes), folded with separately cooked rice and lentils and small accents of cinnamon and cumin, mounded on a platter with more onions and parsley; vegan, serves 6 in 1 hour, best near room temperature.
glance: 3 pounds white onions, about 45 minutes medium-low then 20 more medium-high until deeply browned
3 cups cooked brown or green lentils (not red or French) and 6 cups cooked long-grain rice
faq: What is mujadara?

Simply a mixture of rice and perfectly cooked lentils, spiked with a big dose of caramelized onions and a bit of cumin and cinnamon. Nutritious, satisfying, inexpensive and easy, it's a hearty one-dish meal with Greek yogurt and maybe a cucumber salad, or part of a larger Middle Eastern feast.
Should it be served hot?
It is best close to room temperature, not piping hot.
Why cook the rice and lentils separately?

Many folks cook them together, but the author finds that doesn't give enough control over their relative textures. Mujadara is best when the lentils are tender but not falling apart (use brown or green, not red or French lentils).
What if I don't have time to caramelize the onions?
A hotter and faster fry can also give delicious results, with a sweet brown surface and a little remaining crunch.
Why so little cinnamon and cumin?
The author's taste is that mujadara should be earthy rather than spice heavy, so they're subtle accents. Some readers agree while others prefer much more: the choice is yours.
